best_for: People working with 3D scans or models headed for 3D printing who need a free desktop tool to clean, repair, inspect and convert large triangle meshes.
description:
MeshLab is a research-born 3D mesh tool that won the Eurographics Software Award at the 2017 Symposium on Geometry Processing, for making geometry research software free for others to build on. The project asks that you cite it in papers where you used it.

You can turn a cloud of scanned points into a closed surface with Screened Poisson reconstruction, take measurements from a model, and line up photos on a 3D model to map their color onto it. Finished models can go straight to Sketchfab. To learn, the site points to free YouTube playlists on the basics, the scanning pipeline and cleanup, offers sample meshes to practice on, and sends how-to questions to Stack Overflow.

points.title: Built for raw scan data
points.text: MeshLab comes from the Visual Computing Lab at ISTI-CNR in Italy and is open source under GPL-3.0. It edits, cleans, heals, renders, textures and converts unstructured triangle meshes, the kind that 3D scanners produce, and helps prepare models for printing.

points.title: Scripting moved to PyMeshLab
points.text: Since 2020.12 the command-line meshlabserver is gone. Batch jobs now go through PyMeshLab, a Python library that runs the same filters.

points.title: Double-precision builds exist, but not here
points.text: Release 2025.07 also comes as 2025.07d, built with double-precision floating point, for Windows, Mac and Linux. This listing carries the standard builds only.

points.title: Windows: one 64-bit installer, machine-wide
points.text: There is no Arm64 Windows build. The two most recent records install for the whole machine, while the 2021.07 to 2022.02 records install per user and are marked as able to run silently. The installer registers OBJ, PLY, STL, OFF, FBX and other mesh types. A .zip build and a Microsoft Store version also exist but are not listed here.

points.title: Mac: Apple silicon arrived in 2025.07
points.text: Version 2025.07 added native Arm64 builds for macOS and Linux, so Macs get separate Apple silicon and Intel DMGs. The app installs with its version in its name, as MeshLab2025.07.app.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is x64 only and unverified
points.text: The Flathub package is built for x64 only and Flathub does not mark it as verified. For Arm64 Linux, the project offers AppImages and tarballs on its release page, which are not listed here.

points.title: Infrequent releases
points.text: The latest version, 2025.07, came out in July 2025, after 2023.12. The Windows listing keeps 7 versions, back to 2020.12; macOS and Linux keep only the current one.
